summary: Portage County, WI: 100-foot steel secondary fire tower completed in late 1939 about two miles south of Plover; listed as gone, with no removal record found.

facts.design: 100-foot steel fire tower, secondary type, with an enclosed shelter at the top
facts.status_note: Statewide lookout list marks it Gone; the sources read give no removal date or method

staffing.status: secondary tower, occupied only in periods of extreme fire hazard

events.note: Erection completed about two miles south of Plover; reported in the Stevens Point Journal on December 22, 1939; one of 31 towers under a WPA project

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel tower completed about two miles south of Plover
evidence.quote: Wisconsin conservation department crews have recently completed erection of a 100-foot, steel fire tower about two miles south of Plover.

evidence.supports: second fire tower in Portage County
evidence.quote: It is the second fire tower in Portage county, another being located several miles further south.

evidence.supports: one of 31 towers under a WPA project sponsored by the conservation department

evidence.quote: WPA workers put in footings for the towers, landscaped the sites, built roads to the towers

evidence.supports: state conservation crews did the erection
evidence.quote: Actual erection of the towers was done by conservation department steel workers.

evidence.supports: secondary tower occupied only in extreme fire hazard
evidence.quote: The new tower is of the secondary type and will be occupied only in periods of extreme fire hazard

evidence.supports: primary towers occupied through the summer
evidence.quote: Primary type towers, he added, are occupied continuously during the summer months.

evidence.supports: purpose was to ascertain origin of smoke to the north
evidence.quote: to ascertain the origin of smoke to the north

evidence.quote: from mills at or near Stevens Point

notes_for_editor: Build and design facts rest on one newspaper item (Stevens Point Journal, December 22, 1939) as reproduced on the centraluslookouts page; no second source found. Two WebSearch calls and a per-tower firelookout check (404) found no removal record, so the story says nothing about how or when it came down. Brief access 'unknown' not carried into facts because no source describes access. Brief height_m 30.5 matches the 100-foot figure; brief status 'gone' matches the index row.
